newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian state offers 61 pct of ginning company.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian state offers 61 pct of ginning company.

text.p: The Egyptian state holding company Cotton and International Trade said on Friday it wanted to sell 61 percent of Arab Cotton Ginning in a privatisation IPO worth about 37 million pounds ($11 million).
For two days starting on September 10, it will take applications for 1,143,320 shares, or 51 percent of the company, at a fixed price of 27 pounds a share.
Another 10 percent of the equity, or 224,180 shares, has been set aside for sale to company employees, it said.

The shares on offer to the public are split into two categories -- 919,140 for individual investors and 224,180 for funds and financial institutions. If the demand justifies it, the holding company may sell more shares to individuals.

The holding company said Arab Cotton Ginning made net after-tax profits of 6.620 million pounds in the financial year ending June 30 1996, compared with 11.146 million in the previous year. It will pay a dividend of 2.00 pounds a share for 1995/6, against 2.65 for the previous year.
It forecast that the company's net after-tax profits would rise to 6.853 million in the current financial year and to 7.341 million in the year 1997/8.
